config_name: Razer Blade 14 — Ryzen AI 9 365 / RTX 5070, 64GB RAM, 2TB SSD

reviews.quote: A high-quality and fast 14-inch all-rounder; the limitation to the RTX 5070 with 8 GB VRAM is a drawback.
The power of a real gaming PC packed into a luxury ultraportable.
Almost a slam dunk; the big downside is battery life.

praises: MacBook-like rigid CNC aluminum unibody in a gaming laptop — 'the base unit cannot be warped' (NBC)
Improved 1.5mm-travel keyboard much better than older Blade models
64GB soldered RAM is unusual and useful in a 14-inch gaming laptop
Copilot+ Ryzen AI platform with 50 TOPS NPU
complaints: Black anodized surfaces are extreme fingerprint and dirt magnets (NBC con: 'surfaces remain extremely susceptible to dirt')
RAM is soldered on the 2025 AMD model — NBC calls it 'a step backwards' for maintenance
High case temperatures under load; deck near the vents runs hot (NBC: 'case temperatures have increased')
OLED PWM flickering at 960Hz below 100% brightness bothers sensitive users
Long-standing Blade-line wear: anodizing/paint scuffs at lid edges and hinge corners over time

design_philosophy: The Blade 14 is the most compact expression of Razer's aluminum-unibody gaming philosophy — a full RTX 50-series GPU and a calibrated OLED squeezed into a ~1.85kg 14-inch chassis that could pass for a work ultrabook. This Copilot+ Ryzen AI config trades peak TGP for portability and efficiency, targeting gamers who travel.
rating_notes: Inferred from NBC's Blade 16 2025 (87%) with Blade 14 deltas (see 32GB sibling) plus +0.5 productivity and +0.5 ai_ml for 64GB RAM vs 32GB (net ai_ml -0.5). No Blade 14-specific pro score found within budget; weight/battery estimated.
standouts: 64GB RAM in a ~1.85kg gaming laptop — rare for local AI/VM use
dealbreakers: RTX 5070's 8GB VRAM is the bottleneck, not the RAM
